task: VLAN 10 is missing from this switch. Create it and enter its VLAN configuration context.

teaching.hint: The VLAN database is separate from an interface’s access assignment.
teaching.takeaway: Creating the VLAN establishes the local Layer 2 object. It does not automatically move a host port into it or provide a gateway.

task: You are configuring VLAN 10. Give it the administrative name USERS.

teaching.hint: The numeric VLAN ID already exists; now set its label.
teaching.takeaway: USERS is a readable label. The VLAN number, rather than the spelling of this name, identifies tagged traffic across links.

task: The selected switch port connects to an ordinary PC sending one untagged network. Fix the port in access mode.

teaching.hint: Choose the host-facing mode independently of its VLAN number.
teaching.takeaway: Static access mode removes trunk-negotiation ambiguity for this PC port. Its data VLAN must still be assigned separately.

task: The selected port is already in access mode. Move its untagged data traffic into the existing VLAN 10.

teaching.hint: Change the port’s data VLAN, not the VLAN database name.
teaching.takeaway: Verify the access VLAN is active and generate fresh host traffic. A correct VLAN assignment does not correct the host’s IP address or mask.

task: Fa0/1 serves an IP phone with a PC behind it. Data must stay in access VLAN 10; put the phone’s tagged voice traffic in existing VLAN 30.

teaching.hint: Add the voice policy without replacing the data VLAN.
teaching.takeaway: The port remains an access port with a voice VLAN. Voice addressing and registration need their own services; this command alone does not establish a phone call.

task: Display the local VLAN database summary, including VLAN status and ordinary access-port membership.

teaching.hint: Inspect the defined VLANs before changing a connected endpoint’s address.
teaching.takeaway: Check that the intended VLAN exists and is active. A port can retain an assigned VLAN number after that VLAN is deleted, without normal data forwarding.

task: A phone’s attached PC works, but you need to verify Fa0/1’s actual data and voice VLAN settings and port mode. Display the detailed switchport view.

teaching.hint: The VLAN summary does not show every operational switchport setting.
teaching.takeaway: Read administrative mode, operational mode, access VLAN and voice VLAN separately. PC connectivity does not establish that the phone has the intended voice policy.

task: On a supported PoE switch, an AP has no power. Display the shared power budget and per-port power state before changing its VLAN.

teaching.takeaway: Separate a disabled power setting from allocation denial. Check the endpoint’s requirement against both per-port capability and remaining switch budget.

task: A workstation was moved to SW1 Fa0/2. After it transmits, display MAC entries for that port to check the VLAN in which it was learned.

teaching.hint: Filter by the new local access port.
teaching.takeaway: Compare the learned VLAN with the workstation’s approved network. A MAC learned on the wrong VLAN points to a membership problem even when the cable is connected.

task: The selected supported PoE port is configured never to supply power. Its attached AP is compatible and the budget is sufficient. Restore normal detection and allocation.

teaching.hint: Use automatic detection rather than forcing an arbitrary wattage.
teaching.takeaway: Automatic PoE allows compatible-device detection and allocation. Verify the resulting power state; it does not guarantee that the AP’s VLAN or IP service is correct.
